name: Honeywell
description: Honeywell sells engineered equipment, software and services for aircraft, buildings, factories and refineries. Through FY2025 it had four segments: Aerospace Technologies (engines, avionics, wheels and brakes, plus aftermarket parts and repair), Industrial Automation, Building Automation and Energy and Sustainability Solutions (UOP process technology and catalysts). On 2026-06-29 it completed the spin-off of Honeywell Aerospace into a separate Nasdaq-listed company (HONA), after spinning off Solstice Advanced Materials on 2025-10-30 and selling its protective-equipment business in 2025, and it effected a one-for-two reverse stock split. The financial lines below are FY2025 as filed, which still include Aerospace; the remaining company has Building Automation, Process Automation and Technology, and Industrial Automation.

gics.note: The Wikipedia list shows the company as "Honeywell Technologies" as read 2026-09-30; the 10-Q for Q2 2026 also uses "Honeywell Technologies" for the post-Aerospace-spin company.

employees.note: Approximately 101,000 employees in 79 countries (about 36,000 in the US), excluding about 19,000 at Sandia and Kansas City National Security Campus operated under DOE contracts.

businessLines.name: Aerospace Technologies (spun off 2026-06-29 as Honeywell Aerospace, HONA)
businessLines.how: Sells auxiliary power units, engines, avionics, wheels and brakes to aircraft makers (original equipment, one-time with long product life) and then spare parts, repair and overhaul to airlines and operators (aftermarket, recurring), plus defense and space contracts.

businessLines.name: Industrial Automation
businessLines.how: Process control systems and software, sensors, safety gear, warehouse automation and mobile computers sold to refiners, life-science, utilities and logistics customers; hardware sales plus software and services on the installed base.

businessLines.name: Building Automation
businessLines.how: Sells building management products (fire, security, controls) one-time through channels, and building solutions projects and service contracts to building owners.

businessLines.name: Energy and Sustainability Solutions
businessLines.how: UOP licenses refining and petrochemical process technology and sells catalysts, adsorbents and equipment to refiners and petrochemical plants; licence and project revenue plus recurring catalyst replacement.

brands.name: Honeywell Aerospace Inc. (HONA)
brands.note: Spun off 2026-06-29; FY2025 revenue $17,510M, 46.8% of FY2025 net sales

brands.name: Solstice Advanced Materials
brands.note: Spun off 2025-10-30 (discontinued operations in the FY2025 10-K)

whatsNext.text: Reporting realigned into Aerospace Technologies, Building Automation, Process Automation and Technology and Industrial Automation; Aerospace separated
Strategic alternatives under evaluation for Productivity Solutions and Services and Warehouse and Workflow Solutions (held for sale at 2025-12-31)
Acquired Johnson Matthey Catalyst Technologies for $1,750M net of cash acquired
